recipes.name: Broccoli and Ramen Noodle Salad
ingredients_raw: 2 (3 ounce) packages chicken flavored ramen noodles

steps.text: Combine slaw mix, broken noodles, and green onions together in a large salad bowl.
Whisk sugar, vinegar, oil, and ramen seasoning packets together in a small bowl; pour over salad and toss to evenly coat. Refrigerate until chilled.
Top with peanuts and sunflower seeds before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Broccoli and Ramen Noodle Salad
raw_recipe.description: This broccoli slaw with ramen noodles, green onions, peanuts, sunflower seeds, and a simple cider vinegar dressing is crunchy, nutty, and delicious.

video.description: Watch how to turn a bag of broccoli coleslaw into a fun and filling salad. We'll make homemade dressing using ramen seasoning packets for an extra kick of flavor. Toss the broccoli with the dressing and add ramen noodles, peanuts and sunflower seeds for crunch.

review.reviewBody: This was good but I have to agree that the dressing seemed to be missing something. I added some soy sauce, crushed garlic, fresh lime juice and chopped cilantro to give this salad a bit of an extra "kick". It got rave reviews!

Made many times and these changes are just my preferences. I use one uncooked soy flavored ramen noodle bag, not two, and break it up with a mallet first. Don't open bag first! I use about 3 green onions, rice vinegar and sesame oil, amounts as stated. I add roasted sunflower seeds and salted chopped peanuts. I think it tastes great whether you add them at first or last. Keeps well next day. (I love having the sauce ingredients premixed for a quick side dish so I put about 4x the amounts in a marked bottle, shake well and use 1/4 the bottle when I want it. Usually add a bit if slaw is stored overnight.)

This is my favorite salad but My receipe has a couple of variations . Instead of peanuts I use 3/4 cup slivered almonds and 3/4 cup sun flower seeds. I cook the noodles as per the pkg instructions and cut them up small and toss in with slaw and nuts. for the marinade, I bring all ingredients to a boil to combine. Cool to room temp. and pour over salad. I like to make this salad the day before I serve it as I find it rehydrates the broccoli slaw.

Very good, with changes. I have had it prepared as directed by the recipe, but this is a much better dish with some easy additions. I used a package of broccoli coleslaw and a bag of angel hair cabbage. Added extra veggies to give the flavor more depth and added nutrition(chopped red and yellow pepper, half a red onion, minced garlic, minced GINGER and cilantro). I like the more veg less noodle version. Also did half sesame oil, soy sauce crushed red pepper and added a big squeeze of lime. TO DIE FOR. Do not cook the noodles, it is a waste of time and makes it too limp and wet.

Lighten up the dressing. I have loved Broccoli Slaw since the first time I've tried it. I've tweaked the recipe some and it's better and even lighter tasting. 1) Halve the dressing recipe and leave out the flavor packet. Especially when you let this sit, it gets oily. You only need half, but pump up the flavor by adding a flavored oil (orange infused olive oil is nice) and season the dressing with salt and pepper. Add a Tablespoon of soy sauce or tamari. 2) Slivered or sliced almonds is a nice swap. 3) Add madarin oranges (canned in water), craisins and/or golden raisins for sweetness instead of all that sugar. Agree with other reviewers, DO NOT cook the noodles - put everythign together and let sit for 30 minutes before serving to soften the uncooked noodles in the sauce.

Everyone asks for this recipe when they taste it. Recipe is good as is. I make my own broccoli, cabbage, carrot slaw 'cause I like to slice and chop. Next time I also used Oriental Ramen and the seasoning that came with it. Do let it sit overnight. For Oriental used 1/8 cup sesame oil and 1/8 cup sunflower oil instead of vegetable oil. Also used rice vinegar instead of cider.
DO NOT COOK THE NOODLES but do break them up.

5 Stars because it's SUPER easy and fast to make, tastes good, and is versatile. I read through several reviews and took tips from a few. I added juice of 1/2 lime and some sesame oil. I also kept the peanuts off and let people top their salad if they wanted so that the peanuts remained crunchy. This salad is SO good. Thanks for the recipe.

I like this better when you toast the noodles with butter. Saute the broken noodles and seeds/nuts in a few tablespoons of butter. Add the flavor packets from the noodles. This will give it all a ton more flavor.

This is a great summer, crunchy recipe.
I have made it numerous times. You can julienne other veggies into the mix. I have never added that much sugar, however, only 2 TBS, at most. Instead of vegetable oil, I use toasted sesame oil. You can also add sesame seeds. Always one of the 1st to go salads at a BBQ. Double the recipe & keep some home for during the week. Refrigerated, will keep for a week.

This was excellent, but like others, I made a few changes. I don't like the noodles crunchy, so I make the salad the night before (except the nuts- I add those right before eating or those will loose their crunch too.) The dressing softened up the noodles just right for my family. I also replaced the peanuts with sliced almonds and used 3/4 cups sunflower seeds instead of 1 cup. I thought the dressing was great, but I will experiment with adding some soy sauce as suggested by some other reviewers because, hey, why not?

You do *NOT* cook the noodles as I've seen some suggest. The crunch is part of the yummy. My 4-year and 10-year old even ate it!

Definitely up for adding garlic, soy sauce, and fresh lime juice to the dressing for some extra zing (as suggested by Kehunter). No cilantro because my DNA makes it taste like dish soap :)

I make this salad all the time and it never disappoints. I've made it my own by using beef ramen instead of chicken ramen, and I substitute almonds for peanuts. This recipe can be easily doubled for a crowd. So good!
I put in less sugar, pistachios instead of peanuts, and sunflower shoots and it's delicious!
I love the recipe. I swapped broccoli florets for the broccoli slaw; almond slivers for the peanuts; sesame oil for the vegetable oil; and I added crumbled bacon and mandarin orange segments. Yummy!!

This is one of my family's favorite salads.. I always double the sugar,oil and vinegar.And add three packs of ramen. And let mine sit out for the ramen to get al-dente instead of refrigerating it automatically. And it turns out perfect every time..

I made a couple changes, and they were using olive oil instead of vegetable oil and Splenda instead of sugar. This may not be the healthiest salad around, but it certainly is tasty. Many recipes using ramen noodles tell you to discard the seasoning packet, but that seasoning is so very important to this recipe. The ramen did soak up quite a bit of the dressing after refrigerating, so I'll probably make a little more next time. The dressing is flat out delish!
I use two parts sesame oil and one part vegetable oil. I took another reviewer's suggestion and added cilantro too. Everyone loved it.

I’ve been making this for a while now but I use beef ramen and no green onions. I don’t smash the noodles I break them up into little clusters and I use salad toppers like dried cranberry with candied pecans. Mix it all up and about an hour in the fridge and it’s perfect!
I really wanted to like this recipe... It just didn't do it for me. I may or may not try it again.

One of our family’s favorites! I never cook the noodles but I do break them apart with a meat mallet so there are no “gobs” of noodles stuck together. I know the video shows them whole but I feel like the broccoli slaw is plenty of texture. The dressing softens the noodles well. Maybe this will help those disappointed with texture.
